newsitem.title: USA: Valspar sees FY97 revs of $1 billion.
newsitem.headline: Valspar sees FY97 revs of $1 billion.

text.p: Valspar Corp, a paint and coatings manufacturer, said Tuesday it expects to post revenues of $1 billion in the fiscal year ending October, compared with $859.8 million a year ago.
"We're a billion dollar company today," chief executive officer Richard Rompala told investors at a Piper Jaffray investor conference here.
Rompala was referring to a graph showing projected fiscal 1997 revenues for the Minneapolis-based company's four business segments.
The chart showed the company's consumer group would have $340 million in revenues in fiscal 1997. That unit posted $295 million in sales a year ago.
The packaging group should have revenues of $320 million, compared with $235 million a year ago and the industrial group should earn $220 million, compared with $206 million.

The special products group is projected to have $120 million in revenues, down from $124 million a year ago. The decline is because Valspar exchanged its maintenance coatings business, which was part of its special products group, for Ameron International Corp's product finishes business.

Rompala told investors the acquisition of Coates Brothers -- the can coatings and metal decorating inks business of Total SA -- should be completed within 18 months. It has so far acquired the Coates businesses in Europe, the United States, Australia, Hong Kong and China. It plans to acquire the remaining businesses in three stages.

"I think we'll do South Africa first, at least partially," he said. "But it's up in the air whether India will come before Southeast Asia, or vice-versa. The original schedule was five years, but both parties would like to move it up to completion within the next 18 months."
